newsitem.title: USA: Vanguard says 7 funds hurt by muni futures errors.
newsitem.headline: Vanguard says 7 funds hurt by muni futures errors.

text.p: The Vanguard Group of mutual funds, which filed a lawsuit May 5 alleging mistakes in pricing the municipal futures contract, said on Monday seven of its municipal bond funds lost money as a result.

The company filed the lawsuit naming Thomson Publishing Corp, a unit of Thomson Corp, and six municipal bond brokers as defendants. Thomson's Bond Buyer unit prices the contract's underlying index using quotes from the six brokers named.

Brian Mattes, a principal at Vanguard, said in a telephone interview that the lawsuit alleges "failure to discharge contractual duties and negligence in the pricing of the Bond Buyer municipal bond index on Dec 19, 1995."
"As a result, the seven portfolios suffered a financial loss," Mattes said.
Mattes said the company would have no other statement, but a copy of the lawsuit obtained by Reuters said the losses were at least $3.25 million.

Vanguard said the seven funds involved were: the Vanguard Municipal Bond Fund, the Vanguard Fixed Income Securities Fund, Vanguard Admiral Funds, the Vanguard New York Insured Tax-Free Fund, the Vanguard New Jersey Tax-Free Fund, the Vanguard Pennsylvania Tax-Free Fund, and the Vanguard Ohio Tax-Free Fund.
The lawsuit said Vanguard held 3,420 municipal futures contracts on Dec 19, 1995, the same day the Federal Reserve lowered short-term interest rates 25 basis points.

Vanguard alleges that the settlement price for the expiring contracts failed to capture the market's strong reaction to the Fed's move, resulting in a settlement price that did not reflect the true market.

The Bond Buyer index "did not catch up with the bond market until the next day, December 20, 1995, when the rest of the bond market changed little from the previous day's close but the (Bond Buyer index) rose 1-4/32," the lawsuit said.

Also named in the suit were the six brokers the Bond Buyer uses to price the 40 bonds in its index: Cantor, Fitzgerald Municipal Brokers Inc; Chapdelaine & Co; J.F. Hartfield & Co; J.J. Kenny Drake Inc; Municipal Partners Inc, and Titus & Donnelly Inc.
Thomson officials were not available for comment on the lawsuit.
Officials with the six brokerage firms either had no comment or were not immediately available.
